column1: # word_list.tsv: terms for scripts/check_style.py. Columns: term<TAB>guidance<TAB>replacement.
# A term field can hold variants split by '|' (the first is shown in messages). Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive;
# a capitalized hit in mid-sentence is skipped unless the term itself has capitals (proper nouns).
# Adapted from the word list of the Google developer documentation style guide (CC BY 4.0), paraphrased.
# The rows after the word-list rows are terms that came up often when the skill was tested.
# A guidance that starts with "skill row" is a term Google's list doesn't cover; the skill added it.
# Skipped table entries that say avoid or don't use, because a literal whole-word match would misfire on correct text:
#   abort: common API and signal term
#   above: context-dependent; handled by the position rule in the script
#   below: context-dependent; handled by the position rule in the script
#   access (verb): noun use is fine; handled by a context pattern in the script
#   canary: define if used; no mechanical test
#   careful, carefully: plain English, but too common in warnings to flag mechanically
#   check (checkbox): only wrong in checkbox sense
#   compliant: use with caution; no mechanical test
#   cons: also an identifier; only the phrase pros and cons is clear
#   first-class: legitimate in language docs (first-class functions)
#   functionality: use with caution; too common
#   health check: use with caution; no mechanical test
#   latest: fine when anchored by a version or date
#   method: generic use, no mechanical test
#   once (after): context pattern in the script
#   since (reason): context pattern in the script
#   while (contrast): context pattern in the script (info-level)
#   will: fine for real future events
#   type (keys): context pattern in the script
# Table entries that only state a spelling or usage rule (one word, hyphenation, 'use X') are left to the script's pattern checks or not checked.
